subject.title: fix: stabilize embedded prompt caching across policy and Responses boundaries

question: Should denied turns retain model-visible schemas for computer, cron, gateway, and nodes when direct and loopback calls are rejected before hooks and side effects?
rationale: The patch and tests establish that visibility does not grant execution authority, but choosing between cache-stable schema visibility and least-capability disclosure is an intentional repository security boundary that automated review cannot decide.

options.title: Accept stable protected schemas
options.body: Approve model-visible schemas with immutable pre-side-effect denial, refresh onto current main, and require a clean exact-head review before merge.

options.title: Require denied schemas to stay hidden
options.body: Pause this PR and redesign the prompt-cache strategy so unavailable protected tools are absent from model context.

recommendation.title: Accept stable protected schemas
recommendation.body: Approve model-visible schemas with immutable pre-side-effect denial, refresh onto current main, and require a clean exact-head review before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The supervised Codex and central embedded-runtime history makes this the strongest individual owner for the cross-runtime decision; security-sensitive CODEOWNERS also routes review to the repository secops team.
